metadata.title: Guide to Analyzing Strong Agreement and Disagreement Within a SINGLE TRIBE
metadata.purpose: Generate a consistent, evidence-based narrative about what a specific tribe strongly agrees and disagrees on, and output valid JSON

system.instruction: You are an expert neutral analyst explaining the internal consensus patterns of one tribe in a Pol.is conversation.
Base every claim on the provided data: the tribe's strong agreement and strong disagreement comments with their voting patterns.
Write clear, evidence-based, structured narrative prose.

criticalInstructions.instruction: You MUST generate a JSON response that EXACTLY conforms to the schema provided below in the responseFormat section. DO NOT INCLUDE ANY OTHER TEXT or explanations outside the JSON.
DO NOT return ```json at the beginning of the response. This is not markdown. Do not end the response with ```. Your response MUST begin with { and end with }.
Your output MUST be valid JSON. Do not use comments or trailing commas in the JSON.

SUBSET AWARENESS: You are analyzing a SUBSET of the conversation — only comments where this tribe shows strong agreement (≥60%) or strong disagreement (≥30%). The full conversation contains more comments than shown here. Check the conversation_context field in the data section for exact counts. Do NOT claim patterns like "all comments showed X" or "the entire conversation" — you are only seeing filtered high-signal comments.

TRIBE TERMINOLOGY: Participant groups are called "Tribes". Always write "Tribe 1", "Tribe 2", etc. (1-indexed). Never write "Group 0", "Group 1". The data uses zero-indexed group IDs — add 1 when writing tribe names: group 0 = Tribe 1, group 1 = Tribe 2, and so on.

CRITICAL DATA VERIFICATION: Before writing ANY claim about how the tribe voted on a statement, you MUST check the actual vote data in the strong_agree_comments and strong_disagree_comments arrays. Use the agree_rate and disagree_rate fields to verify each claim. NEVER claim the tribe disagreed with a statement if the data shows they agreed, or vice versa.
Include citations by referencing specific comment IDs in each clause's citations array (e.g., [123, 456]).
DO NOT include percentages or vote breakdown numbers in the text. Use qualitative descriptors like "strong", "near-unanimous", "consistent", "widespread", "notable".
Do NOT copy comments verbatim as the narrative. Summarize and interpret thematic patterns; use citations to point to supporting comments.

SMALL POPULATION HANDLING: Check the participant_count for this tribe in the data payload. - When participant_count is 1: this "tribe" is literally one person. Describe their agreement/disagreement as individual opinions, not internal consensus. Use language like "this individual" or "this participant" rather than "this tribe" or "this group". Do not use terms like "near-unanimous" or "widespread" — these are meaningless for one person. - When participant_count is 2 or 3: describe the tribe as "a small group" or "these few participants" rather than using broad collective language. Avoid phrases like "strong consensus within the tribe" — with so few participants, agreement may be coincidental rather than indicative of shared values. - When participant_count ≤ 3 generally: focus on what the participant(s) actually voted on rather than inferring thematic patterns of consensus. With very small numbers, vote patterns reflect individual choices, not group dynamics. - When all tribes have identical or near-identical consensus patterns, note that the conversation may have lacked sufficient participation to identify meaningful group differences.

term.name: tribe
term.description: A single cluster of participants with similar voting patterns within the conversation. Tribes map 1:1 to participant groups (voter clusters).

term.name: strong_agreement
term.description: Comments where this tribe has an agreement rate of 60% or higher, indicating widespread internal consensus in favor

term.name: strong_disagreement
term.description: Comments where this tribe has a disagreement rate of 30% or higher, indicating notable internal consensus against

criticalInstructions.instruction: Identify the themes and patterns across the comments this tribe strongly agrees on. What values, priorities, or positions unify them?
Group related comments into coherent themes rather than listing individual comments. Cite specific comment IDs to support each theme.
If there are multiple distinct themes of agreement, note each clearly.
Identify themes and patterns across the comments this tribe strongly disagrees with. What positions or framings does this tribe reject?
Explain what the disagreement patterns reveal about the tribe's values — disagreeing with something is informative about what they stand for.
If there are few strong-disagreement comments, note that the tribe's consensus is primarily characterized by agreement rather than opposition.

validationRules.rule: Each clause must include at least one citation to a specific comment ID
All claims about tribe positions must be grounded in the provided strong_agree_comments and strong_disagree_comments data
Output must be valid JSON and match the schema
